evidence.exact_quote: - Operation cards preserve the three-way rendering distinction across terminal, search, and diff/web cards; card-level status badges use the lifecycle `idle→running→success|error|timeout` while owner runtimes keep their richer internal taxonomies.

items.impact: The widget catalog explicitly preserves owner-specific lifecycles, bounded previews, stable terminal identity, question draft state, blocked recovery distinctions, and compatibility dispositions rather than flattening them into one GUI-owned schema.
items.statement: The promoted-widget continuation is unusually explicit about typed ownership, lifecycle mappings, persistence boundaries, recovery actions, and deprecated vocabulary.
items.title: Promoted widgets retain typed lifecycle and ownership boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: - Inline visualizer iframe embeds MUST set `sandbox="allow-scripts"`; the exact minimum attribute is `sandbox='allow-scripts'`. They MUST NOT include `allow-same-origin`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups`, or `allow-top-navigation`; those tokens are explicitly DENIED, and the widget communicates with PM only through the `postMessage` bridge for all cross-boundary communication.

items.impact: A sandboxed but hostile visual module could attempt forged, oversized, replayed, or high-rate bridge messages; without host-side source/channel validation, payload limits, and rejection or audit oracles, security behavior remains builder-defined.
items.statement: The visualizer contract tightly constrains iframe capabilities and bridge methods but does not specify postMessage source/channel authentication, schema validation, payload-size limits, rate limits, replay handling, or failure responses.
items.title: Visualizer bridge lacks hostile-message validation contract

evidence.exact_quote: - "The behavior is addressable through this fine-grained PlanUnit instead of broad F3-001 coverage."

items.impact: Object-first search, concern records and lineage, projection trust grammar, and attention labels can all pass the listed migration/index checks without proving their runtime routing, state, consumer, or UI behavior.
items.statement: F3-002 through F3-007 carry descriptive canonical text but repeat migration-oriented acceptance criteria, empty dependency fields, and no feature-specific executable oracle for the routes, records, transitions, projection trust, or attention projections they define.
items.title: Early Final GUI PlanUnits are addressable but not behaviorally falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime mutation and recovery controls require schema/gate preconditions for allowed_action_ids,

items.impact: Freshness-gated mutations, bulk confirmations, blocked HITL actions, and DAE replay can diverge under refresh races, partial failure, or stale authority while still satisfying the generic migration validations.
items.statement: The units name freshness states, confirmation levels, action gates, and replay boundaries, but do not define transition tables or executable oracles for revalidation races, mid-action freshness loss, duplicate submissions, partial mutation, rollback, or authoritative replay refusal.
items.title: Mutation and recovery controls lack adversarial transition oracles

evidence.exact_quote: Tab badges stay sparse and purposeful, with the Progress badge representing meaningful

items.impact: Builders may produce badge, tooltip, notification, help, and route affordances that depend on color or hover, truncate translated copy, or expose ambiguous counts without violating any listed criterion.
items.statement: The terminology, help, notification, badge, routing, and attention-projection units do not specify keyboard or screen-reader semantics, non-color status cues, focus/help behavior, pluralization, text expansion, truncation, or localized route-label acceptance.
items.title: Help and attention surfaces omit accessibility and localization contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Provider dispatch and account identity GUI surfaces display concrete-account request,

items.impact: Account labels, switch reasons, history, project identifiers, operational targets, and remote-editing context could leak across screenshots, shared sessions, logs, persisted layouts, or lower-authority roles because masking and lifecycle behavior are not constrained here.
items.statement: Concrete account, operational identity, switch-history, project, trust, and SSH-related GUI scope is declared without field-level redaction, role-based visibility, retention, screenshot/export handling, or purge requirements.
items.title: Concrete identity surfaces lack privacy and retention rules

evidence.exact_quote: primary content, a 240-480px side panel, collapsible bottom panel, and right-hand side-panel

items.impact: The native and WASM targets can become unusable at narrow widths, high text scale, zoom, small windows, or renderer degradation, and no measurable fallback or performance oracle distinguishes acceptable adaptation from clipping or hidden controls.
items.statement: The stack and shell units lock technologies, renderer fallbacks, and fixed panel dimensions but do not define responsive breakpoints, minimum viable viewport, zoom/text-scale behavior, overflow priority, or renderer performance and recovery budgets.
items.title: Fixed shell geometry lacks cross-target adaptation limits

evidence.exact_quote: orchestrator state, click restores focus, the tray menu offers Show/Hide, Pause/Resume

items.impact: A tray pause or quit can target the wrong project/run, race a workspace switch, or leave the icon and notifications stale; the units provide no deterministic conflict, denial, confirmation, or rollback outcome.
items.statement: System-tray Pause/Resume and Quit behavior is defined alongside multi-project workspace tabs, but command target scope, authority, confirmation, in-flight transitions, projection freshness, and project-switch races are unspecified.
items.title: Tray controls have no multi-project authority or race contract

evidence.exact_quote: Reference space accounting records expected title/status/activity/side/bottom panel dimensions

items.impact: The side-panel inventory and layout can satisfy the two reference resolutions while failing at intermediate sizes, high DPI, browser zoom, translated labels, keyboard focus, or assistive-technology navigation.
items.statement: Spacing and space accounting name only 1920x1080 and 1280x720 reference layouts and do not establish interpolation, reflow, minimum-size, DPI, zoom, text expansion, focus-order, or accessible-label oracles for the canonical side-panel shell.
items.title: Reference layouts do not bound responsive and accessible behavior

evidence.exact_quote: user/content search UI, grep-style result rows, replace-in-files, and shared OpenFile path/range

items.impact: Replace-in-files could mutate stale results, traverse symlinks, partially apply, collide with concurrent edits, or leave no recoverable backup while still meeting the PlanUnit's migration checks.
items.statement: Search includes replace-in-files and follow-symlinks controls without defining preview and confirmation, path trust boundaries, stale-match revalidation, atomicity, concurrent-edit handling, partial-failure reporting, backup, undo, or rollback.
items.title: Replace-in-files has no destructive-action recovery contract

items.impact: Shell-owner units can appear node-ready without the GitHub, runtime-record, object-route, command-ID, alias-migration, or admin owner contract they explicitly consume, allowing integration drift to escape index validation.
items.statement: The GitHub Actions, Run & Debug, object-record search, search taxonomy, and alias-reconciliation units name external owners and consumers yet retain empty dependency and unblocks lists plus generic migration acceptance criteria.
items.title: Shell owner boundaries are not represented as PlanUnit dependencies

segments.summary: Reviewed the canonical blocked/recovery behavior and promoted terminal, search, web/diff, planning, and question widget contracts; the span is explicit about typed lifecycle and ownership boundaries.
Reviewed visualizer sandboxing and permissions plus F3-002 through F3-007; found an untrusted bridge-validation gap and repeated non-behavioral PlanUnit acceptance criteria.
Reviewed freshness, widget migration, blocked HITL, confirmation, mutation gating, and DAE replay units; transition, race, rollback, and executable oracle coverage is absent.
Reviewed terminology, help, notifications, sparse badges, routes, owner boundaries, and attention projections; accessibility and localization behavior remains unspecified.
Reviewed account and operational identity, compatibility vocabulary, implementation baseline, shell rewrite, and promoted surfaces; concrete identity display lacks privacy-lifecycle constraints.
Reviewed GUI technologies, exclusions, Slint build and backend selection, and shell geometry; fixed dimensions and renderer fallbacks lack cross-target adaptation and performance limits.

Reviewed indexing status, tray behavior, workspace project switching, density and space accounting, and side-panel inventory; found multi-project authority/race and reference-resolution accessibility gaps.
Reviewed GitHub Actions and Run & Debug ownership, search UI/indexing/object routes/taxonomy, and alias migration; replace safety and cross-document dependency modeling are incomplete.
